about.title: Who I am
bio: I’m a Computer Science student. My recent work spans browser-side prompt compression, an edge incident response dashboard powered by local Ollama models.
I coordinate technical projects for FOCES CEC.

experience.title: Where I’ve worked & trained
summaries: Coordinate engineering projects and technical workshops for the student computer science association.
Organize hackathons and community build sessions across campus.
Connect engineering peers with open-source roadmaps, hackathons, and technical bootcamps.
Engineered an on-device incident response dashboard with a three-person team during a 10-hour hackathon.
Integrated local Ollama LLMs to classify simulated attacks and output actionable firewall rules without cloud APIs.
Conducted web vulnerability assessments, OSINT recon, and active network penetration labs.
Deployed controlled phishing simulations with Gophish and mapped network perimeters with Nmap.
Built TortoiseLang (slowlang) — a satirical programming language and IDE enforcing typing cadence with real-time velocity monitoring and ASCII feedback.
Won first place at TinkerHub Useless Projects 2.0 for creative software engineering and humorous event-driven architecture.

projects.title: Things I’ve built
taglines: A language that punishes fast typing
Cyber threat dashboard with local AI
Tray app that hides title bars of maximized windows
descriptions: Satirical Python-like language and Tkinter IDE that enforces a 30 WPM typing cap. Type faster and the ASCII turtle rage-locks you out for 2 seconds, then mocks you in haiku. The zero-install web demo plays by the same rules.
Full-stack event manager built for the FOCES Volunteer Project. FastAPI + Pydantic backend with two endpoints, live search filter and localStorage persistence on the front end. Live on GitHub Pages.

Volunteers log impact across six tracks at 10 points per journal entry, earning titles from their top three. Express 5 REST API behind bcrypt hashing, 7-day JWTs and three rate-limit tiers: 300, 120 and 20 requests per 15 minutes.

Simulated SOC dashboard: streaming attack-log feed, a one-button incident workflow, copyable iptables mitigations and an auto-generated CISO post-mortem. Optional analysis via local Ollama (qwen2.5:3b), with static fallbacks for five threat types.

Compresses prompts in-browser for ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini: regex pre-clean plus a five-stage optimizer, fully local and network-free. Ollama or the containerized companion joins only past 280 characters, racing a 3-second deadline.

One 695-line C# file on the Win32 API: polls the foreground window every 50 ms and parks maximized title bars 40 px above the screen edge. Mouse to the top 2 px slides the bar back down; Ctrl+Alt+S pauses, Ctrl+Alt+T toggles per app.

a11y.title: Accessibility statement
a11y.lede: This portfolio is designed to be lightweight, semantic, and navigable by keyboard, touch, and assistive technologies.
a11y.semanticBody: All interactive elements use standard native elements (<button>, <a>, <nav>) with explicit labels, roles, and focus outlines.
a11y.contrastBody: Both dark and light color palettes adhere to WCAG AA contrast thresholds across all typography and interactive states.
a11y.motionAfter: settings, disabling non-essential animations for users with vestibular sensitivities.
